Hon'ble Siddharth,J.
Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
Order on Criminal Misc. Application (Leave to Appeal) No. of 2024.
1. Heard Sri Prem Shankar Prasad, learned A.G.A. for the appellant and Sri Zain Abbas, learned counsel for the respondents.

2. The above noted Leave to Appeal Application has been filed in government appeal noted above filed against the judgement and order of acquittal passed by Additional Sessions Judge, Court No.14,
State Of U.P. vs Utkarsh Agrawal And 2 Others on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188734350/
1 District Kanpur Nagar, vide order dated 23.12.2022 in Session Trial No. 45 of 2020 (State of U.P.
Vs. Utkarsh Agrawal), arising out of Case Crime No. 69 of 2019, under Section 498A, 304B, 506 IPC, Police Station Kohna, District Kanpur Nagar.
3. The prosecution story in brief is that the complainant gave a written report at Police Station concerned stating therein that complainant has solemnized marriage of his daughter namely Harshita Agrawal on 24.01.2017 with Utkarsh Agrawal, respondent no. 1.

1 District Kanpur Nagar

sentences.text: In the marriage complainant spent about Rs. 40 lakhs but the in-laws of the deceased were not satisfied with the dowry and demanded further dowry in the shape of Rs. 25 lakhs in cash and due to non fulfillment of the same they started harassing and torturing her continuously.
On 06.07.2019 the deceased made a telephonic call to the complainant informing that her in-laws have made a plan for committing murder.
Thereafter the complainant reached the place of his daughter and persons gathered there told the complainant that in-laws of the deceased had thrown her from the window due to which she died.
On the basis of the aforesaid, first information report of the present case was registered and the investigating officer after due investigation has submitted charge-sheet.
4. The accused-respondents denied the prosecution allegations and claimed to be tried.

5. The prosecution in order to prove its case has examined PW-1 Constable, Hemlata Shakya; PW-2,
Padam Kumar Agrawal (complainant); PW-3, Smt. Santosh Agrawal; PW-4, Virag Karvariya; PW-5,
Gopal Narayan Dwivedi; PW-6, Constable Amod Kumar; PW-7, Om Prakash; PW-8, Manish Agrawal; PW-9, Ravindra Prasad; PW-10, Ajit Singh Chauhan; PW-11, Rohan Ganeriwal; PW-12,
Smt. Gitika Ganeriwal; PW-13, Dr. Pravin Kumar Srivastava; PW-14, Kamal Kumar Ganerwal;
PW-15, Smt. Shakuntla and PW-16, Rajendra Kumar.

6. The learned Trial Court has acquitted the accused-respondents holding that the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond all reasonable doubt and as such the accused-respondents are entitled for acquittal.
7. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that trial court has misread the evidence on record and wrongly acquitted the respondents.

8. The appellate Court is usually reluctant to interfere with a judgment acquitting an accused on the principle that the presumption of innocence in favour of the accused is reinforced by such a judgment.

The above principle has been consistently followed by the Constitutional Court while deciding appeals against acquittal by way of Article 136 of the Constitution or appeals filed under Section 378 and 386 (a) Cr.P.C. in State of M.P. Vs. Sharad Goswami,(2021) 17 SCC 783; State of Rajasthan Vs. Shera Ram, (2012) 1 SCC 602, Shivaji Sahabrao Bobade Vs. State of Maharastra,
(1973) 2 SCC 793.
9.

State of Gujarat, (1996) 9 SCC 225 has observed that the High Court must examine the reasons given by the trial Court for recording their acquittal before disturbing the same by re-appraising the evidence recorded by the trial court.

entities.text: Ramesh Babulal Doshi Vs. State of Gujarat, (1996) 9 SCC 225
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
For clarity, para 7 is extracted herein below:
State Of U.P. vs Utkarsh Agrawal And 2 Others on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188734350/
2

entities.text: State Of U.P. vs Utkarsh Agrawal And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "Before proceeding further it will be pertinent to mention that the entire approach of the High Court in dealing with the appeal was patently wrong for it did not at all address itself to the question as to whether the reasons which weighed with the trial Court for recording the order of acquittal were proper or not.
Instead thereof the High Court made an independent reappraisal of the entire evidence to arrive at the above quoted conclusions.

This Court has repeatedly laid down that the mere fact that a view other than the one taken by the trial Court can be legitimately arrived at by the appellate Court on reappraisal of the evidence cannot constitute a valid and sufficient ground to interfere with an order of acquittal unless it comes to the conclusion that the entire approach of the trial Court in dealing with the evidence was patently illegal or the conclusions arrived at by it were wholly untenable.

While sitting in judgment over an acquittal the appellant Court is first required to seek an answer to the question whether the findings of the trial Court are palpably wrong,
manifestly erroneous or demonstrably unsustainable.
If the appellant Court answers the above question in the negative the order of acquittal is not to be disturbed.

Conversely, if the appellant Court holds, for reasons to be recorded, that the order of acquittal cannot at all be sustained in view of any of the above infirmities it can then - and then only - reappraise the evidence to arrive at its own conclusions.
In keeping with the above principles we have therefore to first ascertain whether the findings of the trial Court are sustainable or not."

10. The Supreme Court in the case of Sadhu Saran Singh Vs. State of U.P., (2016) 4 SCC 357 has observed that an appeal against acquittal has always been on an altogether different pedestal from an appeal against conviction.

entities.text: Sadhu Saran Singh Vs. State of U.P., (2016) 4 SCC 357
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In an appeal against acquittal, where the presumption of innocence in favour of the accused is reinforced, the appellate court would interfere with the order of acquittal only when there is perversity.
11. The Supreme Court in the case Basheera Begam Vs. Mohd. Ibrahim, (2020) 11 SCC 174 has held that the burden of proving an accused guilty beyond all reasonable doubt lies on the prosecution.

entities.text: Basheera Begam Vs. Mohd. Ibrahim, (2020) 11 SCC 174
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
If,
upon analysis of evidence, two views are possible, one which points to the guilt of the accused and the other which is inconsistent with the guilt of the accused, the latter must be preferred.
Reversal of a judgment and other of conviction and acquittal of the accused should not ordinarily be interfered with unless such reversal/acquittal is vitiated by perversity.

In other words, the court might reverse an order of acquittal if the court finds that no person properly instructed in law could have, upon analysis of the evidence on record, found the accused to be "not guilty".
When circumstantial evidence points to the guilt of the accused, it is necessary to prove a motive for the crime.

However,
motive need not be proved where there is direct evidence.
In this case, there is no direct evidence of the crime.

12. The Supreme Court in the case of Kali Ram Vs. State of H.P., (1973) 2 SCC 808 has observed as under:
"25.

entities.text: Kali Ram Vs. State of H.P., (1973) 2 SCC 808
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Another golden thread which runs through the web of the administration of justice in criminal cases is that if two views are possible on the evidence adduced in State Of U.P. vs Utkarsh Agrawal And 2 Others on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188734350/
3 the case, one pointing to the guilt of the accused and other to his innocence, the view which is favourable to the accused should be adopted.

entities.text: State Of U.P. vs Utkarsh Agrawal And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This principle has a special relevance in cases wherein the guilt of the accused is sought is to established by circumstantial evidence."

13. The Supreme Court again examined in State of Odisha v. Banabihari Mohapatra & Ors, (2021) 15 SCC 268 the effect of the probability of two views in cases of appeal against acquittal and held that if two views are possible on the evidence adduced in the case, one pointing to the guilt of the accused,
and the other to his innocence, the view which is favourable to the accused should be adopted.

entities.text: State of Odisha v. Banabihari Mohapatra & Ors, (2021) 15 SCC 268
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. The Supreme Court in Sujit Biswas v. State of Assam, (2013) 12 SCC 406 has reiterated the position that suspicion, however strong, cannot replace proof.

entities.text: Sujit Biswas v. State of Assam, (2013) 12 SCC 406
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accused is presumed to be innocent unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.

15. In the background of the law discussed herein above, we will examine the trial court's findings and evidence adduced during the trial by the witnesses to test the legality and validity of the impugned order.
16. After hearing the rival contentions, we find that the prosecution case was not supported by prosecution witnesses of fact.

PW-2, informant and father of the deceased gave an application before the trial court stating that he has lodged the F.I.R. against the respondents due to anger and grief suffered by his daughter's death but respondents never harassed her for demand of any dowry.
PW-11, brother-in-law of the deceased (Jeeja) and PW-12, sister of the deceased also did not supported the allegations of demand of dowry from family members of the matrimonial home of deceased.
PW-15, who was an employee in the house of the respondents did not support the prosecution case.
PW-16, who used to visit to the house of the deceased and was an employee of her father also did not stated anything supporting the prosecution case.

17. Learned counsel for the State has submitted that PW-9 who is resident of the same apartment as of the deceased, stated that on 30.06.2019 he went to the apartment of the respondents where he heard the respondents reprimanding the deceased for not bringing any dowry and asking her to talk to her father and bring dowry thereafter he went to Tata Nagar and was not present in his apartment when the incident took place.

Demand of dowry by the respondents was fully proved by PW-9.
18.

Learned counsel for the respondents submitted that PW-3 has admitted that Rs. 14, 40,000/-
was transferred by the respondent No. 3, Smt. Ranu Agarwal in the account of the informant PW-2.

He has submitted that apart from this amount, money in cash was also given by respondents to the informant which he was not returning and because of his conduct the deceased felt humiliated in her matrimonial home and committed suicide by jumping from her flat on seventh floor of her apartment.

19. After hearing the rival contentions and going through the record, we are of view that the judgment and order of the trial does not suffers from any illegality and the counsel for the State is unable to demonstrate any perversity in the findings recorded by learned trial court in the judgment State Of U.P. vs Utkarsh Agrawal And 2 Others on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188734350/
4 and order of acquittal.

sentences.text: 20. Hence this leave to appeal application is rejected.
Order on Government Appeal 1.
Since leave to appeal application has been rejected, therefore, the above noted government appeal is, hereby, dismissed.
2. Let this judgment be notified to the trial court and its record be returned within two months.
